title: Digital Wallet
oneLine: Process wallet commands through deterministic partitioned state machines, replicate immutable events with consensus, expose CQRS read models, and coordinate cross-shard transfers with a recoverable saga or TCC.
opening: A wallet transfer has two legs and must preserve conservation of value: debit and credit cannot be lost or duplicated. I would expose an idempotent transfer command and route each account to a partition whose leader runs a deterministic state machine. The leader validates balance and emits immutable debit/credit ledger events, replicated through Raft before acknowledgment. CQRS read models materialize balances and history from the event log; snapshots speed recovery but the events remain authoritative. When both accounts share a partition, one local transaction applies both legs. Cross-partition transfers use a durable orchestrator with TCC or saga semantics: reserve/debit first so intermediate state cannot be spent, then credit, and compensate/recover from every phase. Phase state, fencing, retries, and out-of-order messages are explicit. Reconciliation and replay continuously prove balances and event history agree.
ask: Wallet-to-wallet transfer only, or deposit/withdrawal/FX too?
Is synchronous finality required or can transfer be pending?
What audit, replay, and availability guarantees?
scale: Each transfer produces at least two account postings; 1M transfers/s implies 2M+ ledger events/s before replication.
Partition by account ID, but colocate related accounts only if a stable business grouping reduces cross-shard transfers.
Single partition throughput is bounded by sequential consensus/state-machine work; scale through many independent Raft groups.

decisions.default: Immutable double-entry events/ledger plus materialized balance read model.
decisions.why: Replay, audit, and historical proof are first-class wallet requirements.
decisions.switch: A transactional relational ledger may be simpler at moderate scale; event sourcing should not be adopted without deterministic tooling.

decisions.default: Per-partition consensus/Raft for ordered durable events.
decisions.why: A wallet cannot accept ambiguous divergent balances from AP replication.
decisions.switch: Asynchronous replicas can serve stale history, but authoritative writes go through the leader/quorum.

decisions.default: Orchestrated saga/TCC with debit/reserve before credit and durable phase table.
decisions.why: It avoids global 2PC locks while ensuring intermediate funds cannot be spent twice.
decisions.switch: Use 2PC only in a tightly controlled database system where latency/availability trade-offs are accepted.

decisions.default: Commands may fail; accepted events are deterministic facts and never call external I/O during replay.
decisions.why: Reproducibility requires the same event sequence to produce the same state.
decisions.switch: External decisions must be captured as explicit input events with their evidence/version.

deepDives.title: TCC/saga safety
points: Persist coordinator phase before sending operations and use idempotent operation IDs.
Debit/reserve first; crediting first creates spendable money during partial completion.
Handle cancel-before-try and duplicate/out-of-order commands with phase/version checks.

deepDives.title: High-performance event sourcing
points: Append sequentially to a local WAL/event store, keep hot state in memory/RocksDB, and snapshot periodically.
Replicate the event log—not merely the cache—through consensus.
Use single-writer event loops and batching, but preserve durability and observability.

deepDives.title: CQRS and client receipt
points: Write acceptance and read-model visibility are different milestones.
Return transfer ID/status; reverse proxy/gateway can wait or push completion without polling every partition.
Balance response includes version/sequence so clients know freshness.

deepDives.title: Proof and reconciliation
points: Sum postings per currency must be zero across system accounts.
Replay event log into a shadow state machine and compare balances/snapshots.
Code upgrades run against historical events to detect semantic drift before rollout.

failures.risk: Coordinator crashes after debit before credit
failures.response: Recover durable phase, query idempotent operation status, continue credit or compensate according to state machine; funds remain reserved/unspendable.
New Raft leader has committed log; client retries same transfer ID and receives existing state.
Expose status/version, allow leader/consistent read for critical confirmation, and monitor projection lag.
Stop affected partition, replay in shadow with fixed deterministic code, compare, then rebuild projection or append correction events—never edit history silently.

questions.a: Both use local transactions and compensation. TCC explicitly reserves in a try phase and can execute branches in parallel; saga is an ordered sequence with rollback. Choose from latency, resource reservation, and domain complexity—not fashion.

questions.q: Why not Redis balances for 1M TPS?
questions.a: Redis can deliver throughput, but simple sharded counters do not provide cross-shard atomicity, durable audit, deterministic replay, or financial reconciliation. It can serve read models/caches, not be the entire correctness story.
No account spends more available funds than allowed, every transfer has balanced debit/credit postings in one currency, and each business command affects the ledger at most once.

questions.q: How do you scale a hot account?
questions.a: One account’s authoritative ordered writes are inherently serial. Use batching/netting, product limits, subaccounts with controlled aggregation, or dedicated partition capacity; do not pretend hashing removes the ordering constraint.

mistakes: Calling event sourcing a replacement for accounting invariants
Using eventual consistency for spendable authoritative balance
seniorSignal: State conservation-of-value and no-double-spend invariants first. Then explain deterministic state machines, consensus boundaries, cross-shard phase recovery, read-model lag, and proof by replay/reconciliation.
implementation: Partitioned Java event-loop services with Raft-backed append logs
Saga/TCC coordinator with durable phase table, idempotent operation IDs, and fencing
CQRS balance/history projections, reconciliation, and shadow replay tooling
